answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before earning trust-weighted rewards. The bond stays at risk through a challenge window, so creating identities multiplies capital tied up; detected collusion forfeits it. Reviewers can check this costly commitment without trusting account names. A spiral of fake accounts cannot cheaply harvest rewards across an ocean of identities: even a falcon-fast attacker pays the capital and opportunity cost for each bond.
